title: Convergent Inhibitory Cortical Circuit Disruption Drives Genetically Distinct Absence Seizures.
abstract: Using stargazer and tottering mice, two absence epilepsy models carrying point mutations in distinct genes altering pre- and postsynaptic transmission, the authors show that a translaminar inhibitory circuit motif defined by layer 6 corticothalamic neurons and a Tac1 interneuron subtype is selectively disrupted in both models. This early functional defect was followed by synaptic collapse of deep-layer somatostatin interneurons coinciding with seizure onset. Chemogenetic disruption of the L6 CT-Tac1 motif alone in wild-type mice was sufficient to induce both the secondary interneuron collapse and emergence of spike-wave discharges.
